solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fishing, immediately catches this tiddler?

indicators.note: the run of words catches and holds the answer inside its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An angler pleased to land a small fish straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' signals the letters running from the end of 'Fishing' into 'immediately'. The question mark admits that 'tiddler' is a stretch for a tiny golf putt.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a very short putt that opponents concede without it being played is a small, trivial thing, hence a tiddler.

clue.text: One scoffing good Brie served crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of Brie go mad and reorder

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at fine cheese laid out on biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits the cheese is served on; it is the anagram signal. 'served' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jibe is a mocking remark; one who gibes or jeers is a scoffer.

clue.text: Muslim festival involving a boy I had got muddled (8, two words)

indicators.note: muddled letters are mixed up, so the whole pool of a, LAD and I had is rearranged

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A confused child losing track of things during a religious celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got muddled' scrambles A + LAD + IHAD into the two-word answer, Id al-Adha.
explanation.definitionFit: Id al-Adha, the feast of sacrifice, is one of the two major festivals in the Islamic calendar.

clue.text: Small atolls tsunami got? Could be giant ones

indicators.note: says that the letters of tsunami got could be rearranged into the answer plus the word giant

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a tsunami swallowed little islands, and whether huge ones went too.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of TSUNAMI GOT equal the answer plus GIANT; take GIANT away and rearrange the remaining S, U, M, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A motu is a small reef islet of a Pacific atoll; the plural names several of these little coral islands.

clue.text: Had meal below joined grinding stone

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first in the grid

parts.note: met as in joined or came together with
to have eaten a meal is ate

explanation.surface: Eating, after which friends met up at a quern.
explanation.definitionFit: A metate is the flat stone on which maize and grain are ground by hand in Mexico and Central America.

clue.text: Eastern monarch after throne's peculiarly magnetic

indicators.note: the eastern monarch follows the rearranged letters
peculiarly means oddly, so the letters of throne's take a strange new order

parts.note: the word throne's with its s counted as a letter
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: An oriental ruler's seat of power has a strange attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiarly' gives NORTHS from the throne's letters, and 'after' places the eastern monarch last. The answer describes the pole of a compass needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-seeking pole of a magnet is the end that points northward, a property of magnetic things.

clue.text: Inveterate tourist, swine after goblet's drunk

indicators.note: the swine comes after the rearranged goblet
drunk means intoxicated, so the letters of goblet stagger into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter
a swine is a contemptible person, a rotter

explanation.surface: A heavy-drinking traveller, a pig of a man, after draining his cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is the anagram signal, giving GLOBET; 'after' sets the swine last. The surface drinker and the swine are both misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter travels the world constantly, the very type of a habitual sightseer.

clue.text: Groundwork, soft, unaltered

parts.note: B marks a soft (black) pencil lead
as is means in its present state, unchanged

explanation.surface: Preparatory work left soft and untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil leads are graded B for soft, H for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation on which something is built, which groundwork also lays.

clue.text: Quiet backwater, one joining muskeg?

parts.note: muskeg is North American swampland, so a bog by example
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A peaceful creek that runs into a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' just links AN to BOG. A bogan is a Canadian term for a sluggish side stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Canada a bogan is a still, slow side channel of a river, a quiet stretch of water.

clue.text: Early harvest in Angola yielding gum ingredient

indicators.note: the harvest is put in the Angolan code letters

parts.note: AN is the international vehicle registration code for Angola
rabi is the spring grain harvest of India and Pakistan, gathered early in the year

explanation.surface: An early crop in an African country turning out a sticky product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' is a link meaning producing. Rabi, an Urdu-derived word, is the crop sown in autumn and reaped in spring in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabin is the main soluble constituent of gum arabic, so it is a component of that gum.

clue.text: It's played in ragas

indicators.note: played as in played about with, so the letters of in ragas are reworked

explanation.surface: Naming an instrument heard in Indian classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the sarangi, a bowed Indian string instrument, is played in ragas.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarangi is a short-necked bowed instrument central to Hindustani classical music, where ragas are performed.

clue.text: Post dialectally translatable as 'posto'

indicators.note: the letters of posto can be translated, or turned, into a rearranged form

explanation.surface: A note that a regional word for post renders an Italian-looking term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posto' looks like Italian for a post or place; it is just the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In some dialects a stoop (also stoup) is a post or pillar, so it is a regional word for post.

clue.text: Dye, cobalt, seeped inside a great deal

parts.note: Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt

indicators.note: the seeping goes inside the great deal

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
ran as dye runs or seeps

explanation.surface: A lot of cobalt dye leaked through.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN goes inside LOT, after the chemical symbol CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A colorant is any substance used to colour something, which is what a dye does.

clue.text: Questionable club cricketer at the wicket with no score

parts.note: the batter is the cricketer facing the bowling at the wicket
O, zero, is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A batsman out for a duck at his club, his place now in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Questionable' is part of the definition: the word is a doubtful Shakespearean form, possibly a misprint, so its sense of cudgel is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare Shakespearean word taken to mean a cudgel, its reading doubtful, so a dubious name for a club.

clue.text: Clothes, old — Victorian rubbish

parts.note: garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Old clothes from the nineteenth century are mere junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' means from the Australian state of Victoria, not the 1800s: garbo is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo is Australian slang for garbage or a garbage collector, so rubbish in an Aussie state.

clue.text: Chemical used in purifying contaminated ale tun

indicators.note: contaminated means spoiled or tainted, so the letters of ale tun are disordered

explanation.surface: A cleaning agent needed for a cask of tainted beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tun is a large brewer's cask; 'contaminated' rearranges ALE TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: An eluant is the solvent used in chromatography to wash substances out, a step in separating and purifying them.

clue.text: Subtropical fruit, less OK, chef served after syrupy cake

indicators.note: the reduced chef is served after the cake

parts.note: a baba is a small cake soaked in rum syrup

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letters named are taken out

parts.note: a cook is a chef
the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A chef in a bad mood dishes up exotic fruit after a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes the named letters from the chef, and 'served after' places what is left behind the cake. The babaco comes from Ecuador.
explanation.definitionFit: The babaco is a seedless relative of the papaya grown in subtropical highlands, its fruit eaten fresh.

clue.text: E.g. Marley (dead) reappears and Scrooge trembles, alarmed initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: The ghost of dead Marley returns in A Christmas Carol and Scrooge quakes in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Dickens's ghost Jacob Marley; the definition is Bob Marley, the reggae singer and Rastafarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was a devout Rastafarian, so he is an example of a follower of that faith.

clue.text: Liverish about wind getting up in Maidenhead?

indicators.note: the liver colour goes around the turned wind

parts.note: puce is a liver-coloured purplish brown

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A bilious traveller troubled by a strong wind in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns the wind to ELAG, which 'about' encloses. Maidenhead is a Berkshire town, but here it means virginity.
explanation.definitionFit: Pucelage is an old word for virginity, which maidenhead also means.

clue.text: Violet (American) tends Rod, poorly, in grip of fever (12, apostrophe)

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are held inside the fever

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever

indicators.note: poorly means unwell, so the letters of tends Rod are out of order

explanation.surface: Rod is ill with a fever, and someone nurses him back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges TENDSROD into DDERSTON, which goes 'in grip of' AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In America the dogtooth violet, a lily with violet-like flowers, is called by this name.

clue.text: Repair work, task involving disorderly inn

indicators.note: the task wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: darg is a Scots and dialect word for a day's work or task

indicators.note: disorderly means messy, so the letters of inn are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fixing up a rowdy pub is quite a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' jumbles the inn to NIN, and 'involving' wraps the task round it. Darg is a Scots word solvers meet mostly in barred puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning is mending holes in fabric with stitches, a kind of repair.

clue.text: Sconce for one retiring from dictionary work?

parts.note: Chambers is the dictionary used by Azed and many cryptic setters
tick means to work or function, as a clock does

explanation.surface: Someone giving up lexicography is asked what lamp to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reads as leaving work but means going to bed; a sconce is a candlestick.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short candlestick with a handle, carried to light the way to the bedroom.

clue.text: E.g. Prospero hides identity in crisis time for author?

indicators.note: the magician conceals the identity inside himself

parts.note: Prospero, in The Tempest, is a magician or mage
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: The Tempest's magician conceals who he is when Shakespeare faces a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The author is Shakespeare, whose word this is for middle age, the time of a midlife crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean term for middle age, the period associated with a midlife crisis.

clue.text: Place round WC all upside-down — prepare with kit to fix it? (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
the placing goes round the toilet

parts.note: put means to place
a loo is a WC

explanation.surface: A toilet turned over needs someone with tools to set it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' gives PULOOT, and 'all upside-down' turns the lot. The definition's 'to fix it' plays on the upturned WC.
explanation.definitionFit: To tool up is to equip oneself with the necessary tools, ready for a job.

clue.text: Throw up once having ingested slice of mushroom — do so frothily?

indicators.note: the old vomiting word swallows the letter

parts.note: spue is an old spelling of spew, to vomit

indicators.note: a slice from the front of the word mushroom, its first letter

explanation.surface: Eating a bad mushroom leads to violent, foamy sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the archaic spelling SPUE; 'having ingested' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spume is to foam or froth, so it means spewing out in a frothy way.

clue.text: Way of proceeding on minor peak requires such nerve

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of proceeding
a tor is a small rocky hill

explanation.surface: Climbing a small hill takes a certain courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nerve' suggests daring, but the definition means a type of nerve fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor nerve carries impulses to the muscles, so this word is the kind of nerve described.

clue.text: Patriarch, English, captivated by Stirling?

indicators.note: the English letter is held captive inside the driver's surname

parts.note: Stirling Moss was a famous British racing driver

explanation.surface: An Englishman enchanted by a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirling' looks like the Scottish town but stands for Sir Stirling Moss, the British racing driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and is honoured as a patriarch of the Hebrew people.

clue.text: Trim last off excessive body matter

parts.note: trim means slim

indicators.note: the last letter off, or from, the word excessive

explanation.surface: Cutting the final part off an overweight body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' reads as an instruction to cut; it is the adjective meaning slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is the soft clay-like matter of which, in poetic usage, the human body is made.

clue.text: State are centrally denied approval for council

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for state is refused and removed

parts.note: to say is to state
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
a nod signals approval

explanation.surface: A country whose middle is refused consent for a governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is the metric unit of area (100 square metres), abbreviated A, not the verb; dropping it from the middle of SAY leaves SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a governing assembly of church officials, a kind of council.

clue.text: Crude dwelling producing nasty smell — tidy inside

indicators.note: the tidying goes inside the smell

parts.note: ponk is a variant of pong, a stink
do, as in do up, means tidy

explanation.surface: A rough hut gives off a stench that cleaning might fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link. Ponk, a variant of pong, is in Chambers; the dwelling is South African.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa and Malaysia a pondok is a roughly built hut or shack.

clue.text: Patterned lace — Judy's famous clanger?

definitions.meaning: a bobbin lace with a pattern outlined in thicker thread
a variant spelling of the streetcar in Judy Garland's song that went clang, clang, clang

explanation.surface: Some lace, and a gaffe made by a famous Judy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clanger' reads as a blunder but means a vehicle that clangs; Judy Garland sang about it in Meet Me in St Louis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a patterned bobbin lace and, as a spelling variant, a tram or streetcar.

clue.text: You may find this Christian is out of place in Tunisia

indicators.note: says the letters of Tunisia, with those of is out, are put in a different place, rearranged

explanation.surface: A believer who feels like a misfit in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: TUNISIA has the letters of the answer plus IS; remove I and S and rearrange TUNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uniat is a member of an Eastern church in communion with Rome while keeping its own rites, so a Christian.

clue.text: Romance includes this sexiness, Alison so going for it!

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: one thing goes and another takes its place

parts.note: the name as written
the letters as printed
a, the indefinite article, stands for an unspecified thing, it

explanation.surface: A love affair that includes allure, with Alison urged to seize her chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for' means one piece is replaced by another inside the name. Alison is the name of Azed's wife, hence the jokey exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is one of the Romance languages descended from Latin.

clue.text: Perrier? Chap, faint, given litre

parts.note: a man is a chap
gone as in passed out, fainted

explanation.surface: A man drinking bottled water passes out, then gets a litre more.
explanation.walkthrough: Perrier is a bottled water, but here a perrier is a medieval stone-throwing engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangonel is a medieval catapult for hurling stones, the same kind of siege engine as a perrier.

clue.text: George wretchedly abandoning love for fly-by-night?

indicators.note: wretchedly means miserably or poorly, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter drops out of George

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Poor George dumps his girlfriend and does a moonlight flit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning love' removes O from GEORGE; 'wretchedly' rearranges GERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An egger is a moth, a creature that flies by night.

clue.text: Benny Hill went at this!

definitions.meaning: slang for an amphetamine tablet, as in a Benzedrine pill
racing driver Graham Hill, or his son Damon, drove at great pace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Benny Hill' looks like the comedian, but split it: Benny is drug slang, and Hill is the racing driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is slang for amphetamine, the drug in a benny, and also means great velocity.
